objectives: Segment fl-words into phonemes before spelling.
Write f and l in the correct order for the initial blend.
Spell flap, flip, flop, flag and flat accurately.
Read back each spelling to check the vowel and ending.
concepts: Encoding maps heard phonemes to graphemes in order.
Both /f/ and /l/ must be represented in an fl-word.
The rime determines the vowel and ending spelling.
Read-back helps detect missing letters or an incorrect vowel.

definitions.definition: Represent spoken sounds with written graphemes.
Separate a spoken word into phonemes in order.
Read a written word after spelling it to check it matches the target.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct “fag” when the target is flag.
workedExamples.solution: Add l after f to represent the second consonant: flag.

commonMistakes: Leaving out l and spelling flap as fap.
Confusing the short vowels in flip, flop and flap.
Using only the first letter as a cue.
Not reading the completed word back.
keyTakeaways: Segment the full word before writing.
Keep f and l in order at the beginning.
Use the correct vowel and ending for each word.
Read the spelling back and self-correct.

conceptual.prompt: Why must l be written after f in flap?
conceptual.answer: Because /l/ is the second phoneme in the blend.

conceptual.prompt: What should you do before spelling?
conceptual.answer: Segment the whole word into phonemes in order.
To check that every sound and grapheme matches.

application.prompt: Correct “fag” when the target is flag.
Spell the word with onset fl and rime -at.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How do you choose between flap and flip?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Listen for the vowel: short /a/ in flap and short /i/ in flip.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What is wrong with spelling flap as fap?
How do sound boxes support fl spelling?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They help keep each phoneme in order so /l/ is not omitted.

mixedReview.prompt: Which word ends in /g/: flag or flap?

mixedReview.answer: Read the word back and check every sound.

activities.name: Segment and spell fl-words.
steps: Move one counter for each phoneme.
Write graphemes in order, including f and l.
Read the spelling back and check the vowel and ending.

activities.name: Repair incomplete fl-word spellings.
steps: Review examples such as fap for flap or fag for flag.
Identify the missing or incorrect grapheme.
Read it back and explain the correction.

outcomes: Spell taught fl-words with both initial consonants.
Self-correct an omitted l or an incorrect vowel.
Read back a spelling to verify it.

options: Segment all phonemes and map them in order

answerKeys.explanation: Flap represents all four phonemes in order.
Segmentation helps preserve the full sound sequence.
The /l/ represented by l is missing.
The initial blend is written fl.
Read-back helps detect missing or incorrect graphemes.
Flip uses short /i/, while flap uses short /a/.
The blend needs both consonants in sequence without an extra vowel.
